dedupe_keys.name: north american power grid and communication network anomalies for several magnetic storms usgs data release

description: This USGS data release by J. J. Love and B. S. Murphy (2022) compiles lists of operational interference to electricity power grids and communication networks in the United States and Canada during magnetic storms. Four lists cover the storms of March 1989, August 1972 and March 1940 and various storms from 1946 to 2000, and a fifth summarises geomagnetically induced current statistics for 1969-1972. Entries come from published papers, technical documents and research reports and give a brief description of each anomaly, the storm, and where known the utility, facility and start and end times; latitude and longitude were added from a Department of Homeland Security list of power-grid facilities, georeferenced paper maps or internet maps. It was published on 17 March 2022 to support assessment of magnetic-storm impacts on grid and telephone systems, alongside a Space Weather paper (doi 10.1029/2021SW003030). The files are CSV tables (1989, 1972, 1940, other anomalies and GIC statistics) with metadata, accessible online at no cost through ScienceBase. Caveats: source reports are incomplete and uneven, locations are estimated, and the lists end in 2000. It supports historical event analysis and space weather hazard exposure studies of power grids and telecom networks; related records are the NRCan space weather effects chronology, the Hydro-Québec 1989 case study and the USGS geomagnetism observatory data.
